cases.question: What happens if a team uses an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception in a trade that would put Apron Team Salary over the Second Apron Level?

claims.text: A trade using an Aggregated Standard Traded Player Exception that would put the team's Apron Team Salary over the Second Apron Level is prohibited.

cases.question: When is a player still eligible for NBA Most Valuable Player if he did not play sixty-five Regular Season games?

claims.text: A player who did not play at least sixty-five Regular Season games can still satisfy the MVP eligibility criteria if he (A) played in at least sixty-two Regular Season games, (B) suffered a "season-ending injury," and (C) played in at least eighty-five percent (85%) of the Regular Season games played by his Team prior to suffering that injury.

A "season-ending injury" for this purpose is an injury that, in the opinion of a physician jointly selected by the NBA and Players Association, makes it substantially more likely than not that the player would be unable to play through the May 31 following the date of the injury.

Separately, a player who fails to satisfy the Award Eligibility Criteria in a Season may nonetheless be deemed eligible for MVP if he prevails in either an Award Eligibility Grievance or an Extraordinary Circumstances Challenge for that Season.

To prevail in an Award Eligibility Grievance, the player must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the Team willfully limited his minutes played or games played during the Regular Season with the intention of depriving him of award eligibility.

For counting toward the games-played criteria, a player is considered to have played in a Regular Season game if he played at least twenty minutes of that game, except that for no more than two Regular Season games per Season a player counts as having played if he played at least fifteen but fewer than twenty minutes.

cases.question: How does the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception change above the Second Apron Level, and which transaction table covers that limit?

claims.text: The Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is listed in row K of the Transaction Restrictions Table, and row K’s Applicable Apron Level is the Second Apron Level.
The table that sets this limit is the Transaction Restrictions Table in Section 2(e)(4).

Under Section 2(e)(2)(i)(A), a team may not engage in a Transaction Restrictions Table transaction if, immediately after the transaction, its Apron Team Salary would exceed the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to that transaction.

Under Section 2(e)(2)(i)(B), a team that engages in such a transaction may not, for the remainder of the Salary Cap Year, have an Apron Team Salary exceeding the Applicable Apron Level corresponding to that transaction.
The Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception also requires that the team’s Apron Team Salary immediately after using the exception exceeds the First Apron Level.

Once a team has signed a player using the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception, it may not engage in rows A through E of the Transaction Restrictions Table in 2023-24, or rows A through F for each Salary Cap Year beginning with 2024-25.

cases.question: What counts toward the cap as Salary, and how is Team Salary determined?

claims.text: A player's "Salary" for a Salary Cap Year is his Compensation for the Season covered by that Salary Cap Year, plus any other amount deemed to constitute Salary under the Agreement. It excludes Unlikely Bonuses, benefits received under the Agreement (such as Article IV benefits, per diem, and moving expenses), and any portion of Compensation attributable to another Salary Cap Year; it also includes any consideration received by a retired player that is deemed Salary under Article XIII.

"Team Salary" for a Salary Cap Year is the sum of all Salaries attributable to a Team's active and former players plus other amounts computed in accordance with Article VII, less applicable credit amounts computed in accordance with Article VII.

Article 7, Section 4(a) provides that, in computing Team Salary, all of the listed amounts are included, beginning with the aggregate Salaries of all active players (and former players to the extent the Agreement provides) attributable to a particular Salary Cap Year, subject to the rules of Article VII.
The Salary Cap, which Team Salary is measured against, is the maximum allowable Team Salary for each Team for a Salary Cap Year, subject to the rules and exceptions in the Agreement.

cases.question: How much is the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception?

claims.text: For the 2023-24 Salary Cap Year, the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is $5 million.

For each subsequent Salary Cap Year, the Taxpayer Mid-Level Salary Exception is $5 million multiplied by a fraction whose numerator is that Salary Cap Year's Salary Cap and whose denominator is the 2023-24 Salary Cap.

cases.question: An Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent has a prior regular salary of 10000000 and the prior average player salary is 12000000. What is the first-year cap under the veteran free agent exception?

claims.text: For an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent, the first Salary Cap Year may provide up to the greater of (A) 175% of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year of the prior Contract, plus 175% of any Likely and Unlikely Bonuses, or (B) Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses totaling 105% of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year.
Applying the stated inputs: 175% of 10,000,000 is 17,500,000, while 105% of 12,000,000 is 12,600,000; the greater amount is 17,500,000, so the first-year cap is 17,500,000 (absent bonuses).

cases.question: What is the first-year salary cap for an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent under the veteran free agent exception?

claims.text: Under the Veteran Free Agent Exception, an Early Qualifying Veteran Free Agent’s new contract may provide in the first Salary Cap Year up to the greater of (A) 175% of the Regular Salary for the final Salary Cap Year of his prior contract plus 175% of any Likely and Unlikely Bonuses called for in that final year, or (B) Salary plus Unlikely Bonuses totaling 105% of the Average Player Salary for the prior Salary Cap Year, subject to Article II, Section 7.

cases.question: What does Salary include, and does it include Unlikely Bonuses?

claims.text: Salary is defined, with respect to a Salary Cap Year, as the player's Compensation for the Season covered by that Salary Cap Year plus any other amount deemed to constitute Salary under the Agreement; it also includes consideration received by a retired player that is deemed to constitute Salary under Article XIII.

Salary does not include Unlikely Bonuses, nor player benefits under the Agreement (such as Article IV benefits, per diem, and moving expenses), nor any portion of Compensation attributable to another Salary Cap Year.
Consistent with that exclusion, the CBA elsewhere treats Salary and Unlikely Bonuses as separate amounts that are added together, rather than including Unlikely Bonuses within Salary.

cases.question: What can't a second-apron team do in a trade?

claims.text: Beginning with the 2024-25 Salary Cap Year, the Second Apron Team restrictions apply to a team that is a Second Apron Team for a Salary Cap Year (i.e., a team whose Apron Team Salary exceeds the Second Apron Level as of the start of its last Regular Season game in that Salary Cap Year).

A Second Apron Team is prohibited from trading (conditionally or unconditionally) its first round draft pick in the first NBA Draft that occurs following the seventh Season that follows the Season occurring within such Salary Cap Year.

For the four Salary Cap Years immediately following such Salary Cap Year, if the Team is a Second Apron Team for two or more of those years, that first round draft pick becomes subject to a Draft Pick Penalty (making it the final pick in the first round); if it is a Second Apron Team for fewer than two of those years, the team becomes permitted to trade that pick as of the day following the last day of the Regular Season of the third of those four Salary Cap Years in which it is not a Second Apron Team, and the pick is not subject to a Draft Pick Penalty.
